args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression, and why it was promoted despite being unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001, and the on-call engineer has been paged.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with about 18% of requests erroring. The same build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging, so it reached production despite failing there.
- **Rollback:** I picked v2.3.0 because it's the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions run v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident INC-0001:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It lists two follow-ups: find what broke in v2.3.1, and find out why it went to production while unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
